title: Method X Improves Classification Accuracy on Dataset D

sections.text: We study image classification on the made-up dataset D. The baseline method Y is a small convolutional network. We propose method X, which adds a normalization step. Method X reaches 91.2% accuracy on dataset D (see Table 1).
sections.title: Introduction

sections.text: Method X extends baseline Y with one extra normalization layer. Both models are trained for 10 epochs with a fixed seed of 0 and a learning rate of 0.01. Training method X takes half the time of baseline Y.
sections.title: Method

sections.text: We split dataset D into 800 training and 200 test examples. We also evaluate robustness by flipping 10% of training labels. Dataset E is mentioned for future work and is not available.
sections.title: Experiments

sections.text: Table 1 reports test accuracy on dataset D. Method X reaches 91.2% accuracy and trains 2x faster than baseline Y. Under 10% label noise, method X keeps 89.5% accuracy.
